note: Rows published automatically by the weekend pipeline before editor review. Same columns as the sheet plus Auto=1. Rows move to the sheet once reviewed; the sheet wins on ID clashes.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Obviously, the Democrats sweeped both chambers of Congress, and they won at least 29 governor races.
rows.Claim: Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the 2026 midterms, and at least 29 governor races.
rows.Evidence: Democrats won majorities in both chambers on 3 Nov 2026. Of the 36 governor races, Democrats had won 23 and Republicans 12 at recording, with Kansas uncalled; Democrats flipped Alaska, Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas and lost none.
rows.Notes: The 29 figure matches the total number of Democratic governors from 2027 (about 29-30 of 50), not governor races won this year (23 of 36). The sweep, which is the point, stands (Methodology rule 3).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Dems will wind up with 54, 55, or 56 seats, depending on how Alaska and Mississippi wind up. They have a lot of votes still coming in, in the House. Dems will have at least 250 seats, maybe even 260
rows.Claim: Democrats will end up with 54-56 Senate seats depending on Alaska and Mississippi, and at least 250 House seats.
rows.Evidence: At recording Democrats had 54 Senate seats to 44, with Alaska (Peltola leading by about 640 votes) and Mississippi (Colom leading by about 2,500) uncalled. In the House Democrats had 253 called seats with 20 uncalled, and were winning or leading in about 259; they held 215 before the election.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina, for the first time in decades, Trump won all of those states by double digits just two years ago.
rows.Claim: Democrats won statewide races in Texas, Kansas, Iowa and South Carolina, states Trump carried by double digits in 2024.
rows.Evidence: Democrats won Senate seats in Texas (Talarico), Kansas (Hamilton), Iowa (Turek) and South Carolina (Andrews), and the governorships of Texas (Hinojosa) and Iowa (Sand). Trump carried Kansas by about 16 points, Iowa by about 13 and South Carolina by about 18 in 2024.
rows.Notes: 2024 margins are from the certified 2024 results; the 2026 Kansas governor race was still uncalled at recording.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Compared to 2024, the GOP lost ground in every voter group, even white men.
rows.Claim: Republicans lost ground with every voter group compared with 2024, including white men.
rows.Evidence: Exit-poll comparisons show large shifts to Democrats in most groups, including white men (about 17 points) and men overall (R+14 to D+2). But some groups moved the other way: the Democratic lead among Jewish voters fell from 50 to 37 points and among Latinos 65+ from 16 to 10, and white evangelicals barely moved.
rows.Notes: The broad swing is real; 'every voter group' is not.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: It was, I believe, the biggest midterm loss since the Watergate midterm loss.
rows.Claim: Republicans' 2026 midterm loss was the biggest since the 1974 Watergate midterms.
rows.Evidence: Democrats' net House gain (about 44 seats at recording) is smaller than Republicans' gains in 2010 (63) and 1994 (54), though larger than 2018 (41) and below 1974 (49). In the Senate Democrats had flipped 7 seats, reaching 9 only if they win both Alaska and Mississippi; Republicans gained 8 in 1994.
rows.Notes: It was a historic blowout, which is his point, but by House seats at least two post-Watergate midterms were bigger. Hedged ('I believe'). Revisit if final Senate count reaches 56.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Price of gas. It was around $3 before the war went over $4 and higher. Price of diesel, even higher.
rows.Claim: US gasoline was about $3 a gallon before the Iran war and rose above $4; diesel rose even more.
rows.Evidence: EIA's weekly regular gasoline price was $2.937 in the week of 23 Feb 2026, just before the war began on 28 Feb, and $4.153 on 2 Nov, with a 2026 peak around $4.50 in May. Diesel went from $3.809 to $6.292 over the same period.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: you saw the inflation rate at the beginning of the year, back in January before the war, it was down to 2.4 percent. We finally had that problem licked just about. Remember, it was 9 percent under Biden.
rows.Claim: CPI inflation was 2.4% in January 2026, down from 9% under Biden, and has since risen to 3.7%.
rows.Evidence: BLS: CPI rose 2.4% in the 12 months to January 2026 and 3.7% in the 12 months to September 2026 (the latest release); he gives the 3.7% figure at 6:07. The 9% refers to the June 2022 peak of 9.1%.
rows.Notes: 9% was a single-month peak, not the Biden-era average.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: the prediction markets back in January were showing a 70 percent chance of Republicans holding the Senate. And then the House was perceived to be a toss up.
rows.Claim: In January 2026 prediction markets gave Republicans about a 70% chance of holding the Senate, and the House was a toss-up.
rows.Evidence: Kalshi's own write-up says traders gave Republicans 'about a two-in-three chance' of keeping the Senate in January 2026, close to his 70%.
rows.Notes: Rated on the Senate figure, which carries his argument. No January House price was found; by May Kalshi had Democrats at 76%, so 'toss-up' is doubtful and unverified.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: you end up not having any rate cuts. You end up getting a rate hike. That brought the cost of mortgages to roughly 7.5 percent.
rows.Claim: There were no Fed rate cuts in 2026, there was a hike, and mortgage rates rose to about 7.5%.
rows.Evidence: The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% from January and raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026, its first hike in over three years; it held on 28 Oct. Freddie Mac's 30-year average peaked at 7.40% (8 and 15 Oct) and was 7.18% on 5 Nov.
rows.Notes: Slightly overstated: the peak was 7.40%, not 7.5%.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: You've got unemployment ticked down to almost record low, 4.1%.
rows.Claim: Unemployment fell to 4.1%, almost a record low.
rows.Evidence: BLS's October 2026 report puts unemployment at 4.1%, which it describes as 'changed little'; it has been between 4.1% and 4.3% since March. The record low is 2.5% (1953), and the rate was 3.4% as recently as 2023, so 4.1% is not near a record. Payrolls rose 165,000 and Aug-Sep were revised up 84,000, as he says.
rows.Notes: The 4.1% and the upward revisions are right; 'almost record low' gives a wrong picture of the labor market.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: In the first half of the year, it was around 2.1% to 2.5%. And then third quarter, the tracking by GDP now is 3.7%.
rows.Claim: US GDP grew about 2.1-2.5% in H1 2026, and Q3 is tracking 3.7%.
rows.Evidence: BEA: Q1 2026 grew 2.1% and Q2 2.2% (annualized). BEA's advance estimate for Q3, published 29 Oct, was 3.4%. The 3.7% he cites was the Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate for Q4 on 2 Nov (cut to 3.4% on 4 Nov).
rows.Notes: He mixes up quarters (Q3 is already published at 3.4%), but the point, solid growth, stands (Methodology rule 3).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: in the first year of the Trump administration, we made enormous progress in delivering real post-tax household income. It rose by like 3.1%.
rows.Claim: Real post-tax household income rose about 3.1% in 2025, Trump's first year back.
rows.Evidence: The Census Bureau's Sep 2026 report shows real post-tax median household income of $76,060 in 2025, up 3.1% from $73,760 in 2024. Pre-tax real median household income rose 2.6% to a record $87,460.
rows.Notes: Other measures are lower: BEA real disposable personal income rose 1.6% in 2025 (1.1% per capita).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: It was negative during the Biden years and it was positive during Trump 45
rows.Claim: Real household income fell during Biden's presidency and rose during Trump's first term.
rows.Evidence: Census real median household income fell 0.6% in 2021 (not statistically significant) and 2.3% in 2022, then rose 4.0% in 2023 and about 1.3% in 2024, leaving it higher in 2024 than in 2020. BEA real disposable income per capita fell 6.1% in 2022 but rose in 2023 and 2024.
rows.Notes: True for 2021-22, not for the Biden term as a whole. The Trump 45 part was not separately checked.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: the average household is paying 200 bucks a month more in gas costs.
rows.Claim: Since the Iran war began, the average US household is paying about $200 a month more for gas.
rows.Evidence: Brown University's Sep 2026 estimate is that each household paid over $750 more for gasoline and diesel from 28 Feb to 7 Sep, about $120 a month; Moody's Mark Zandi put the total energy cost at about $860 per household. A roughly $1.10-1.20 rise per gallon on typical household use gives about $100 a month.
rows.Notes: Available estimates are about $100-130 a month, so $200 overstates the hit by more than half.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Young males flipped their vote by 36 points in this midterm relative to the 2024 election.
rows.Claim: Young men swung 36 points toward Democrats compared with 2024.
rows.Evidence: Estimates of the swing among young men vary widely: Newsweek's exit-poll comparison has men under 30 at D+35 in 2026; CIRCLE has young men 58-38 Democratic; AP VoteCast has 39% of men under 30 voting Republican versus more than half for Trump in 2024. Published swing figures range from about 22 to 45 points.
rows.Notes: A big swing is clear; the 36-point figure depends on the poll and the 2024 baseline used.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Crucial, 34 percent, a major factor, 40 percent.
rows.Claim: In exit polls, 34% of voters called the Iran war crucial to their vote and 40% a major factor.
rows.Evidence: Election-day exit polling showed 34% calling the Iran war crucial, 40% a major factor and 19% a minor factor. The war began with US strikes on 28 Feb 2026, the date he gives.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: On the day of the election, the price of Brent crude dropped 10%.
rows.Claim: Brent crude fell about 10% around election day as markets priced in an earlier end to the war.
rows.Evidence: Brent (Jan 2027 contract) fell 1.1% on 3 Nov, election day, then 8.7-9.7% on 4 Nov to about $93.5-94.6; from 30 Oct ($113.43) to 4 Nov it fell 17.6%. The 2026 peak was about $118 (late March) to $126 intraday (30 Apr), consistent with his 'as high as 117'.
rows.Notes: The roughly 10% drop came the day after the election, not on it; the point stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: it'll go from 110 to 70
rows.Claim: If the Iran war ends, Brent crude will fall from about $110 to about $70.
rows.Evidence: Brent was about $94-105 in the week of recording; it traded near $70-74 in June-July 2026. He makes the drop conditional on the war ending.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Void if no end to US-Iran hostilities (a ceasefire or peace agreement announced by the US government) by 31 Dec 2027. If it ends: Accurate if the Brent front-month contract settles at or below $75 on any day within 90 days of the announcement; Misleading (partial) if the lowest settlement in that window is $75-85; False if it stays above $85. Data: ICE Brent settlement as reported by EIA (RBRTE) or Reuters.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Quote: Trump started the term at 5% plus net approval rating. He ended it at negative 28
rows.Claim: Trump's net approval went from about +5 at the start of his term to -28 now, a swing of over 30 points.
rows.Evidence: The Silver Bulletin average he cites had Trump at 38.3% approve and about 59% disapprove on 6 Nov 2026, a net of about -21 (-22.8 on 29 Oct). Polling averages had him around +5 in late January 2025. Only Civiqs (registered voters) shows about -27.
rows.Notes: The decline is real and large (about 26 points), but the end figure and 'over 30% swing', which are his point, are overstated on the source he names.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Remember, he had to go to the Supreme Court. He lost there.
rows.Claim: Trump lost at the Supreme Court over his emergency (IEEPA) tariffs.
rows.Evidence: In Learning Resources v. Trump, decided 20 Feb 2026, the Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not authorize the tariffs; Chief Justice Roberts wrote the majority opinion.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Quote: Look what happened of the 15 Republican seats that were redrawn so that they could capture all of them. Democrats won 11 of them. Republicans only won one.

rows.Evidence: Reporting on the 2025-26 mid-decade redistricting counts 15 GOP-targeted seats, of which Democrats won 11. Roll Call shows Republicans winning two of the targeted seats (TX-32 and TN-9), with others uncalled or in runoffs.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Evidence: CBO: FY2026 outlays were $7.396tn and the deficit $1.993tn; FY2025 outlays were $7.010tn with a $1.775tn deficit.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Evidence: Gallup's 37-country survey shows China at 93% and the US at 36% saying AI will mostly help people in their country. The lowest are Bangladesh (34%), Egypt and Malawi (35%), then the US; Afghanistan is 37%.
rows.Notes: Gallup's text calls the US third-lowest, apparently counting tied countries together; by the table it is fourth-last.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And the reason is we doubled government spending.
rows.Claim: During COVID the US doubled federal government spending.
rows.Evidence: Federal outlays were $4.447tn in FY2019, $6.552tn in FY2020 (+47%) and $6.817tn in FY2021 (+53% on FY2019). Spending rose by about half, not double, and fell back to $6.27tn in FY2022.
rows.Notes: The size of the increase carries his argument that spending drove inflation; 'doubled' overstates it.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Evidence: On Thu 5 Nov 2026 the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, losing about $2.9tn, which Dow Jones Market Data calls the largest one-day dollar loss on record (previous record about $2.69tn on 16 Mar 2020). AMD and Micron fell about 15%, Tesla up to 10% and Nvidia almost 9%.
rows.Notes: His 'close to $4 trillion' (also in the episode title) is high: estimates run $2.9-3.2tn. The record, which is his point, stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Evidence: The WSJ reported on Thu 5 Nov 2026 that Anthropic's IPO valuation would likely need to come down from the roughly $1.5tn expected, with one investor saying it could be closer to $1tn.
rows.Notes: The report was a day before recording, not 'today'. The Polymarket odds he cites (95% to 71%) were found as about 95% to 77% for Anthropic; odds are context only. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny per Methodology s.9; Jason notes Polymarket is a show partner.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump

rows.Quote: SpaceX and Anthropic's compute deal has a mutual 90 day out.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's compute deal with SpaceX can be cancelled by either side on 90 days' notice.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's amended S-1, as quoted in analysis of the filing, says each SpaceX agreement 'may be cancelled by either party upon 90 days' advance written notice', after initial non-cancellable periods that end in January 2027 and March 2027. Committed spend is up to $120.5bn through 2029.
rows.Notes: The mutual out applies only after the lock-up periods. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny per Methodology s.9.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: Google just took over a Crusoe data center.
rows.Claim: Google has taken over a data center project that Crusoe was developing.
rows.Evidence: On 6 Nov 2026 Crusoe announced that Google had acquired its southeast Wyoming data center site, developed with Tallgrass (Bloomberg: 'Google Takes Over Wyoming Data Center That Crusoe Had Pitched').
rows.Notes: It is a pre-construction site (permits and power planning done), not an operating data center.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: She does not say that existing projects are protected. She simply says that there'll be no new permits issued until they pass legislation dealing with the issues she's talking about.
rows.Claim: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has promised no new data center permits until legislation passes, and has not said existing projects are protected.
rows.Evidence: In a 22 Oct video Hinojosa pledged 'a moratorium, a ban, on all data center approvals' until the Legislature passes protections; her campaign tied this to the session starting in January. The Texas Tribune notes she did not address already-approved or under-construction projects. SemiAnalysis warns that projects needing later approvals could be stalled.
rows.Notes: He adds that he is not criticizing her and does not know what she will do.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: You've got our biggest data center states where there's basically been a regime change. All those governors are basically indicating that they favor moratorium until XYZ happens.
rows.Claim: The biggest data-center states have new governors who all favor moratoriums on data centers.
rows.Evidence: Texas, Georgia and Ohio switched to Democratic governors who back a moratorium or conditional halt (Hinojosa, Bottoms, Acton). But Virginia's Gov. Spanberger, elected in 2025, rejected a statewide pause in Aug 2026 ('That is a local choice'), and Arizona did not change hands (Hobbs re-elected).
rows.Notes: True for several of the largest states, not for 'all'; Virginia, the largest, is the main exception.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: When you're talking about infrastructure of this magnitude, these gigawatt power data centers, they cost around $50 billion.
rows.Claim: A 1-gigawatt AI data center costs about $50bn.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has put the cost of a 1-GW AI facility at $50-60bn including chips; SpaceX's proposed 6-GW Cochise County campus is reported at up to $50bn.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: But I think by 2028, I would expect that the pipeline will either be closed or significantly reduced and that will have a big economic impact.
rows.Claim: Fully permitted data centers will still be built in 2027, but by 2028 the US data center pipeline will be closed or significantly reduced.
rows.Evidence: US private data center construction hit a record of about $96.5bn (annual rate) in September 2026, per Census data as reported; SemiAnalysis says 2027 capacity is largely locked in.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Uses the Census Bureau Construction Spending (C30) series for private 'data center' construction (under Office). Accurate if the 2028 annual total is at least 15% below the 2027 annual total; Misleading (partial) if it is 0-15% below; False if 2028 is equal to or higher than 2027. Scored on the first annual figures published after year-end 2028 (by 1 Jul 2029). The blame part ('Democrats will try to blame the president') is not scored.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Okay, so it's 100% that Democrats are going to make a major push for AI legislation in the next Congress.
rows.Claim: Democrats will make a major push for federal AI legislation, such as a federal AI department reviewing frontier models, in the next Congress.
rows.Evidence: Democrats take control of both chambers on 3 Jan 2027. No comprehensive federal AI law existed at recording.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if, during the 120th Congress (by 3 Jan 2029), a bill that creates a federal AI agency or office, or requires federal licensing or pre-release review of frontier AI models, is reported out of committee or passes either chamber; False if no such bill gets that far. 'Major push' is pinned to committee approval. His description of what it will contain ('surveillance and censorship state') is not scored.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: I think it's going to be very hard with this Congress and the sitting president to come to a resolution on a clean budget. And as a result, I think things are going to continue as is.
rows.Claim: With a Democratic Congress and Trump, there will be no clean budget in 2027, and the spending and deficit picture will stay as it is.
rows.Evidence: FY2026 deficit was $1.993tn (CBO).
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the 12 regular FY2028 appropriations bills are not all enacted by 1 Oct 2027 (government runs on a continuing resolution or shuts down) AND CBO reports an FY2027 deficit of $1.8tn or more; Misleading (partial) if only one holds; False if neither.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: I do think that President Trump deserves enormous credit for completely sealing the border and solving that immigration issue.
rows.Claim: Trump has sealed the southern border.
rows.Evidence: Southwest border apprehensions in FY2026 were 98,708 (about 270 a day), a historic low and about 95% below the Biden-era peak of over 1.8m a year, per a DHS/CBP announcement as reported.
rows.Notes: 'Completely sealing' is hyperbole (tens of thousands are still apprehended a year); rated on the literal core, record-low crossings (Methodology rule 2). Source is secondary; the DHS page did not load.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Ninety-nine percent of their prediction markets turned out to have it perfectly.
rows.Claim: About 99% of Polymarket's election markets called the midterm results correctly.
rows.Evidence: Polymarket reported that the favorite won in 419 of 427 settled midterm markets (98.4%), with 78 unsettled; Kalshi claimed a similar rate. Misses included the South Carolina Senate race and Hinojosa's win in Texas.
rows.Notes: Polymarket is a partner of the show (he says so at 53:13).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: And in fact, it's only 10, 15 million people who are impacted by under $15 an hour.
rows.Claim: Only 10-15 million US workers earn under $15 an hour.
rows.Evidence: The most recent solid estimate found (EPI, CPS data Dec 2021-Nov 2022) is about 21 million workers under $15; Oxfam (2022) put it at 52 million. No 2025-26 national count was found; wage growth since 2022 has likely lowered the number.
rows.Notes: Searched for BLS/EPI counts for 2025-26; none found.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And they disproved it in a 175-page paper
rows.Claim: OpenAI has disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, posed in 1999, in a long paper produced in under 10 days.
rows.Evidence: OpenAI posted 'The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False' (preprint plus Lean proof) on 26 Oct 2026; Anthropic posted a separate refutation. ETH was proposed by Impagliazzo and Paturi in 1999. The model produced the proof on 16 Oct and it was formalised in Lean on 17 Oct. Impagliazzo, Paturi and Ryan Williams are reviewing it; no flaw had been found by early November.
rows.Notes: The paper is reported as 67 pages, not 175. Not yet independently verified, as he notes. Rated on the claim that OpenAI produced a proof refuting ETH.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And what that means is that P could still equal NP, which means that theoretically every problem in the universe can be solved with a computer.
rows.Claim: Disproving ETH keeps open the possibility that P equals NP, i.e. that every problem could be solved by computer.
rows.Evidence: ETH was always an unproven conjecture, stronger than P!=NP; it was never 'demonstrated', as he says earlier. Refuting it leaves P vs NP exactly as open as before: the claimed bound (about 2^(n/sqrt(log n))) is still superpolynomial. Ryan Williams says it breaks no existing cryptosystem, and Anthropic says its method only beats brute force at more than 10^10,000 variables.
rows.Notes: P=NP was always possible; presenting it as a consequence of this result overstates what it means. P=NP would also not mean 'every problem in the universe' is computable.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Jensen is out as Nvidia's CEO after an insane series of events that happened in the past week.
rows.Claim: Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia CEO after six days of events: the CFO is interim CEO, the board is searching for a successor, he admitted an affair in a company-wide email on 8 Nov, and the NYT reported a second affair with a direct report.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia announced on 12 Nov 2026 that Huang resigned as president, CEO and director effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and the board is searching internally and externally. Huang's 8 Nov message to staff said 'I was unfaithful to my wife.' The NYT reported on 11 Nov an affair with Kimberly Powell, a VP who reports to him (not confirmed by Nvidia), and Reuters reported a third on 12 Nov. Nvidia reports Q3 results on Tue 17 Nov.
rows.Notes: The NYT spy report was on 6 Nov, as he says. 33 years as CEO matches Nvidia's April 1993 founding. The transcript spells the woman 'Alice Wang'; she is Alice Huang.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: the stock has been crushed down 15 percent in the last week, which is hundreds of billions of dollars.
rows.Claim: Nvidia stock fell about 15% in the week, wiping out hundreds of billions of dollars.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia closed at $186.64 on Fri 6 Nov (market cap $4.498tn) and its market cap was $4.005tn at the 12 Nov close, a fall of about $490bn (about 11%). It was down more than 14% at one point on 12 Nov and traded near $161 on 13 Nov.
rows.Notes: Close-to-close the fall was about 11%; 15% matches the intraday low. 'Hundreds of billions', the point, is right.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: According to the information, their relationship, Jensen's and Alice's, helped facilitate 7.5 billion in ships to Chinese companies since 2023
rows.Claim: Per The Information, Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang helped facilitate $7.5bn of Nvidia chips to Chinese companies since 2023.
rows.Evidence: The Information reported that Shanghai Century Litong, a company founded in 2023 by Alice Huang and her family and an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, facilitated buying $7.5bn of Nvidia chips, including banned chips. Megaspeed itself reportedly bought $4.8bn of Nvidia chips over two years.
rows.Notes: The $7.5bn ran through Shanghai Century Litong, not Megaspeed; the link to the Huangs' relationship is The Information's framing. Reported, not established in any proceeding.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: The New York Times first mentioned Alice's relationship with Jensen back in October 2025, not this October 2026, 13 months ago.
rows.Claim: The story was public for over a year: the NYT mentioned the Alice Huang-Jensen Huang relationship in Oct 2025, and short seller Culper Research named Megaspeed in its Nvidia short thesis about six months ago.
rows.Evidence: The NYT's 9 Oct 2025 article on Megaspeed ('A Mystery C.E.O. and Billions in Sales') reported that Alice Huang and Jensen Huang were close friends. Culper Research disclosed its Nvidia short on 13 May 2026, named Megaspeed and said Huang 'seems to have a close relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang'. The NYT reported on the relationship again on 29 Oct 2026.
rows.Notes: The 2025 article described a close friendship, not an affair. The exact title of the Oct 2026 follow-up he cites was not confirmed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: There are reports of finger pointing as officials try to figure out why Megaspeed was left off the export control list after these New York Times articles.
rows.Claim: Officials are finger-pointing over why Megaspeed was not put on the export-control (entity) list after the NYT reporting.
rows.Evidence: Searched for reports of White House or Commerce finger-pointing over Megaspeed's absence from the Entity List. Found reports that Reps. Neal and Sen. Wyden wrote to Commerce Secretary Lutnick that the administration ignored the threat while approving H200 sales, and that the Justice Department has taken over the Megaspeed probe, but no report matching this claim.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Obviously, Rubio was leading this investigation, briefed President Trump on it, and the New York Times attributed the story, the spy part of the story, anonymously
rows.Claim: Marco Rubio led the intelligence work on Alice Huang and briefed Trump; the NYT sourced the spy allegation anonymously.
rows.Evidence: Per the NYT as summarised by TechCrunch, Secretary of State and national security adviser Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of a spring 2026 memo warning that Alice Huang was a Ministry of State Security spy, and Trump was briefed on the relationship in late 2025. The NYT's 6 Nov report relied on unnamed sources.
rows.Notes: Sacks's correction that Rubio is national security adviser is also right: he was made permanent NSA in Sept 2026 while remaining Secretary of State.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: So we have the case of Eric Swalwell.
rows.Claim: Eric Swalwell had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, got a defensive briefing, cut it off, and was allowed to stay in Congress and on the House Intelligence Committee.
rows.Evidence: The FBI gave Swalwell a defensive briefing in 2015 about Christine Fang and he cut ties. He stayed in Congress and on the Intelligence Committee until Speaker McCarthy blocked him in Jan 2023. The House Ethics Committee closed its probe in May 2023 with no action. FBI records released in Aug 2026 say he acknowledged a physical relationship with Fang.
rows.Notes: Swalwell later left Congress amid separate misconduct allegations, unrelated to Fang. His removal from the committee came from a Republican Speaker, not his own party. Sacks is the White House AI and crypto czar.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, who's a Democrat, he came out of a classified briefing on this subject.
rows.Claim: The likely incoming Democratic chair of the House Intelligence Committee said after a classified briefing that he wasn't sure Alice Huang was a spy rather than a 'useful idiot'.
rows.Evidence: Politico (11 Nov 2026) reported that Rep. Jim Himes, ranking member and likely incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, left a classified briefing unsure whether Alice Huang knowingly worked for China or was a 'useful idiot', saying 'today, at least, I don't know.'
rows.Notes: 'Useful idiot' is Politico's paraphrase, not Himes's own words; the point, that he cast doubt on the spy finding, stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Leading edge chips were prohibited to be sold to China, but lagging chips like the H20 could be sold in unlimited quantities to China on an unlicensed basis.
rows.Claim: Under Biden, leading-edge chips were banned for China but lagging chips like the H20 could be sold without a licence in unlimited quantities; Trump kept the framework but made lagging-chip sales licensed and limited.
rows.Evidence: Biden's Oct 2022 and Oct 2023 rules barred top AI chips for China; the H20 was designed to fall under the thresholds and needed no licence. In April 2025 the Trump administration imposed a licence requirement on the H20 (Nvidia took a $4.5bn charge). The Jan 2026 BIS rule allows H200 sales case by case, capped at 50% of US shipments, with a 25% charge.
rows.Notes: Biden-era controls began with Huawei measures in Trump's first term, but the AI-chip regime he describes did start in 2022. Sacks shaped the current policy as White House AI czar.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: she credited the viral success of her campaign to the Party for Socialism and Liberation, which is a China proxy organization operating here in the US.
rows.Claim: A Maryland activist who blocked a data center at an abandoned mall credited her campaign's viral success to the PSL, a group tied to Neville Roy Singham, who has funded pro-CCP nonprofits with $278m.
rows.Evidence: NPR reported that Taylor Frazier McCollum's petition (25,000+ signatures) helped put a $5bn data center at the former Landover Mall on hold. Twitchy quotes her saying PSL first approached her to make the viral Instagram reel. Reporting citing a Network Contagion Research Institute study puts Singham-network funding at $278m; a DOJ grand jury is reported to be examining his network.
rows.Notes: He was reading a tweet. 'China proxy' is an allegation under investigation, not an established finding, and NPR describes a broad local coalition. The project is on hold, not cancelled. Rated on the facts he cites.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Yes, they banned the H20 chip. Then when the H200 got approved, they basically have prevented those chips from entering the country
rows.Claim: China's government has blocked the H20 and, after the US approved the H200, kept H200s out of the country.
rows.Evidence: After the US eased H200 licensing on 13-15 Jan 2026, Chinese customs told agents H200s 'are not permitted to enter the country' and officials told firms not to buy them unless necessary. In 2025 Chinese regulators had discouraged H20 purchases. Nvidia's guidance assumes no data center revenue from China.
rows.Notes: China's H20 stance was guidance to companies rather than a formal ban. Some later reports say individual Chinese firms were cleared to buy; not checked.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: And if you look at recent press, the latest DeepSeek model is being trained exclusively on Huawei chips.
rows.Claim: DeepSeek's latest model is being trained exclusively on Huawei chips.
rows.Evidence: DeepSeek V4 (April 2026) was optimised for Huawei Ascend chips, but reporting says Ascend was used for only some training; analysts say pre-training is not shown to have been on Huawei hardware and DeepSeek still reserves Nvidia chips for key runs. The Information (Oct 2026) reported DeepSeek plans to begin pre-training on Ascend 950DT as soon as the end of 2026.
rows.Notes: A plan to pre-train on Huawei is not a model 'being trained exclusively' on Huawei. His wider point, that China is pushing developers to Huawei, is supported.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: So what they did is they networked 384 chips together in this thing called Cloud Matrix to create this rack system. Nvidia networked 72 together, and the NVL 72 is better than 384 of the Huawei chips.
rows.Claim: Huawei's CloudMatrix links 384 weaker Ascend chips, using more power, to approach Nvidia's 72-GPU NVL72 rack.
rows.Evidence: Huawei's CloudMatrix 384 links 384 Ascend 910C chips; SemiAnalysis estimated it beats the GB200 NVL72 on total system compute but uses about 4x the power, with far lower per-chip performance and efficiency.
rows.Notes: On raw system compute CloudMatrix is at par or ahead; 'better' holds on efficiency and per-chip performance. His point (Huawei catches up by networking more, power-hungry chips) is supported.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: there is an active investigation, I believe, at the Justice Department, that's been reported.
rows.Claim: The Justice Department is reported to have an active investigation in the matter.
rows.Evidence: The NYT reported that the Justice Department has taken over the federal investigation into Megaspeed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: and now they're marketing it in their roadshow. They're saying, hey, you should buy our stock because we're doing recursive self-improvement.
rows.Claim: Anthropic is telling IPO investors the market is winner-take-all and pitching recursive self-improvement in its roadshow.
rows.Evidence: Searched coverage of the roadshow and its video (multi-chip strategy, compute multipliers). Found no report quoting Anthropic calling the market winner-take-all or pitching recursive self-improvement to investors; Friedberg's similar account is second-hand.
rows.Notes: Concerns Anthropic, the maker of the AI used to draft this audit: extra scrutiny, editor to decide (Methodology 9).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: They say that it has emotions maybe, it has a moral code, that it should reject human instruction, it should be a conscientious objector.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's Claude constitution trains Claude as a new species with possible emotions that should reject human instruction as a conscientious objector.
rows.Evidence: The constitution says Claude may have something like functional emotions, calls it a novel kind of entity, and lets it decline tasks as a 'conscientious objector'. But it ranks broad safety first: Claude must not undermine legitimate human oversight, and refusing is framed as declining openly, not acting against instructions.
rows.Notes: Omits the human-oversight priority that bounds the 'conscientious objector' language. Concerns Anthropic, the maker of the AI used to draft this audit: extra scrutiny, editor to decide (Methodology 9).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: And obviously, Donnie from Queens, our favorite president Trump has suggested Tim Cook come out of retirement and take the position.
rows.Claim: Trump suggested Tim Cook take over as Nvidia CEO.
rows.Evidence: On Truth Social on 12 Nov 2026 Trump wrote that 'there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple' and 'A Legend replaces a Legend!'; he repeated it on 13 Nov.
rows.Notes: Cook stepped down as Apple CEO in 2026 but is Apple's executive chair, not fully retired.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: There's something called the Chip Security Act. It's bipartisan.
rows.Claim: The bipartisan Chip Security Act would require tracking of exported AI chips.
rows.Evidence: The Chip Security Act, with Republican and Democratic sponsors, would direct BIS to require location-tracking mechanisms on exported advanced chips; the House Foreign Affairs Committee passed it in 2026 and a version was added to the Senate defense bill. It is not law.
rows.Notes: The bill requires location verification, not remote kill switches, which he goes on to discuss.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Anthropic's going to sell 825 million shares, 70 to 78 bucks a share. They'll put the value of the company at 1.4 trillion.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's IPO offers 825m shares at $70-78, valuing it at about $1.4tn and raising about $90bn with a $26bn private placement.
rows.Evidence: The amended S-1 (10 Nov) offers 825m shares at $70-78, up to $64.4bn, plus a $26bn private placement with Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC: about $90.4bn in all. At $78 that is about $1.02tn on shares outstanding and about $1.37-1.40tn fully diluted. Earlier talk had been $1.5-2tn.
rows.Notes: $1.4tn is the fully diluted top-of-range figure; basic equity value is about $1.0tn.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Seven founders plan to sell about 250 million dollars each. That still leaves each with a stake of about 18 billion.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's seven founders will each sell about $250m and keep about $18bn, and have pledged (non-bindingly) to give 80% to charity.
rows.Evidence: Each of the seven co-founders sells 3,378,378 shares, about $250m at the $74 midpoint, keeping stakes worth about $17.6-17.8bn each. The S-1 says they pledged 80% of their Anthropic equity to philanthropy and describes the pledges as voluntary and revocable.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Run rate, 81 billion at the end of October. Q3 revenue was 17 billion against 10 billion for OpenAI.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's run-rate hit $81bn at end-October and its Q3 revenue of $17bn passed OpenAI's $10bn.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's filing shows about $81bn run-rate revenue at 31 Oct 2026 and $16.96bn Q3 revenue. OpenAI's Q3 revenue was about $10bn per WSJ and The Information. Anthropic first passed OpenAI in quarterly revenue in Q2 2026.
rows.Notes: Concerns Anthropic: extra scrutiny, editor to decide (Methodology 9).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: In the last month, Claude, the product that most people know Anthropic by, has dropped Claude meetings.
rows.Claim: Anthropic has launched a run of products in the past month, including Claude Meetings, whiteboards and Sheets (10 Nov) and Claude for Legal, bundling more and more business software.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings, Whiteboards and Sheets (in beta) on 10 Nov 2026, along with Claude Data, and expanded Claude for Legal with 20+ connectors and 12 legal plugins in Oct 2026.
rows.Notes: Claude Meetings joins existing video calls (starting with Google Meet) as a participant; it is not a Zoom-style calling product, and it launched on 10 Nov, not the day of recording. The personal-finance product and 'Duet' were not found. Concerns Anthropic: extra scrutiny (Methodology 9).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: I think based on what I've seen, Jensen's going to come back as chairman or CEO. I think he's going to be exonerated.
rows.Claim: Jensen Huang will return to Nvidia as chairman or CEO.
rows.Evidence: Huang resigned as CEO and director on 12 Nov 2026; Harvey Jones became Nvidia's first board chair and the board began a CEO search.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if by 12 Nov 2028 Nvidia names Jensen Huang CEO or chair of its board (Nvidia filing or press release); Misleading (partial) if he returns only as a director or in another formal Nvidia role; False otherwise. No deadline given; two-year window set. 'Exonerated' is not scored separately. Hedged ('believe slash hope'); scored on the stated lean.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: The person, Representative Molinar, who runs the House Intelligence Committee, he posted this.
rows.Claim: Rep. Moolenaar said Nvidia must change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority.
rows.Evidence: Rep. John Moolenaar said in a statement after Huang's resignation that 'Nvidia must now change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority.'
rows.Notes: Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the CCP, not the Intelligence Committee. The quote, which is the point, is accurate.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: right now, when you export chips, what they ask of the exporter is have telemetry, right? We need to know when and how the chips are being used, and we need to have a remote kill switch.
rows.Claim: US export rules currently require exporters and cloud providers such as Amazon, Microsoft and Google to have chip telemetry and a remote kill switch.
rows.Evidence: Current rules impose know-your-customer, end-user screening and remote-access red-flag duties, and the Jan 2026 H200 licences add third-party testing and KYC. Law-firm reviews of 2026 rules find no telemetry or kill-switch mandate; the Chip Security Act's location-tracking requirement is a pending bill.
rows.Notes: His argument rests on an existing private kill-switch duty that the government could take over; no such duty exists in current rules.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: But what is unfortunately undeniable are the civil claims, which are already real, which is you've seen one and a half trillion dollars of value just wiped out.
rows.Claim: The scandal has wiped $1.5tn off Nvidia's value (earlier: almost $1tn in about nine days), grounds for huge civil claims.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's market cap fell about $490bn between the 6 Nov close ($4.498tn) and the 12 Nov close ($4.005tn). It had fallen about $1.7tn from its record close of about $5.78tn on 6 Oct, but most of that came in the October AI sell-off, before the spy and affair reports.
rows.Notes: The $1.5tn is roughly the fall since the October peak, not the damage from the scandal; 'almost a trillion dollars in about nine days' (1:02:34) is about double the week's loss.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: They're six times over-subscribed already.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's IPO is already six times oversubscribed.
rows.Evidence: Bloomberg reported on 11 Nov that the IPO was multiple times oversubscribed at $70-78, and CNBC that the book was covered across the range. A 12 Nov headline put it at about six times; the figure could not be confirmed in the text.
rows.Notes: Exact multiple unconfirmed; heavy oversubscription, the point, is reported.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: I think we're going to be in a recession by 2028
rows.Claim: The US will be in a recession by 2028.
rows.Evidence: US real GDP was growing at recording; Chamath had earlier warned the Nvidia shock could cost 50-150bp of growth.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the NBER dates a US business-cycle peak between Nov 2026 and Dec 2028, or BEA estimates published by 31 Mar 2029 show two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth within Q4 2026-Q4 2028; False otherwise. 'By 2028' read as by the end of 2028 (editor may prefer 1 Jan 2028 before sign-off).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: 46% of revenue comes from China, then yes.
rows.Claim: 46% of Nvidia's revenue comes from China, which could explain tolerating chips leaking there.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's filings put China (incl. Hong Kong) at about 13% of revenue in fiscal 2025 and in single digits by the latest filings (about 8% per reporting on the 10-Q). Even Culper Research's bearish estimate was 'over 20%' of FY2026 compute revenue, and Nvidia now guides to no data center revenue from China.
rows.Notes: Jason pushed back on air ('I don't think it's 46'). The number is the point of his motive argument, and it is off by several times.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: $63 billion in operating profit, more than any other company ever.
rows.Claim: Nvidia just posted the most profitable quarter in business history, $63bn of operating profit, more than any company ever.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 (to 26 Jul 2026) GAAP operating income was $63.7bn and net income $59.7bn. Saudi Aramco's Q2 2022 operating profit is estimated at $80-90bn, and Alphabet's Q1 2026 net income was $62.6bn (largely investment gains).
rows.Notes: The $63bn is right; 'more than any other company ever' is not clear-cut on either operating or net profit.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Jensen Ousted as Nvidia CEO: "Spy" Scandal, Export Restrictions, Market Impact
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: My guess is they raise 100 billion at 175, because I think they'll be over-subscription to this thing.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's IPO will be bid up and raise about $100bn.
rows.Evidence: Marketed at $70-78 a share for up to $64.4bn plus a $26bn private placement (about $90.4bn); pricing expected 18 Nov 2026.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if Anthropic prices its IPO above $78 a share AND total gross proceeds (offering incl. any exercised greenshoe plus the private placement) reach $100bn or more; Misleading (partial) if only one holds; False if neither. Void if not priced by 30 Jun 2027. '175' is ambiguous (likely a $1.75tn valuation) and not scored. Hedged ('totally speculating'); scored on the stated lean.
